body:
_Verify that an audit log or similar allows for non-repudiation of key transactions._

This is not in scope of ASVS. If a logger writes to a database, a remote logging service or to SIEM team, there is no way to validate non-repudiation or integrity for that matter, in context of ASVS. There are other, much broader teams involved. Most with direct access to data stores. This is an outdated control when we move into distributed logging territory. 

Alternative could include, log over TLS. That's about as far as **application** assurance can go here.

Also, this is a duplicate with 8.6 and 8.11

comments.body:
Can you please check the current wording, which I think hits the note we were originally going for:

| **8.10** | Verify that an audit log allows reconstruction of a user's activity. |  |  | ✓ | 3.1 |

It's a level three control, so it's not for everyone. @Sergicles Thoughts?

This still looks like a duplicate of 8.4 which is "Verify that each log event includes necessary information that would allow for a detailed investigation of the timeline when an event happens" right now.

I say we drop 8.10, @vanderaj - I'm not closing this out just to be sure we got this right. Let's jump on the phone and do one more review of all of 8 and I think we got this.

title: 8.10 - potentially outdated control or beyond ASVS scope
